title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p:
I take my pen to address thee, but know not that I have anything that will be interesting or edifying to thee. But as a testimony of my love to you all, am willing to inform thee the feeling that I have had in having so small a share of thy company when thou was in our country. I have often thought if ever you should pay us a visit, I should would make everything give place to thy company. Instead of that it seemed as if I had only saw thee, and had fallen so far short of that satisfaction that I had contemplated. I could hardly reconcile it to be right, but upon considering the matter I believe it was right to attend the Yearly Meeting and think it a favored time. Many dear Friends from other Yearly Meetings was there. Much good council handed forth at the remembrance of which my heart hath been tendered, and think I may say a favored time to many. I earnestly wish to be one of the members that may improve thereby. After the Yearly Meeting was over, we hurried on our way with the pleasing hope of meeting you, but you had past the road two days before me that came into it which was considerable disappointment to us. We came on to John Heals, thy seemed glad to see us. Spoke of your visit being an agreeable one to them
we were favored to get home safe and found them all better than we left them. Father has recovered since the cool weather much faster than he did while it was warm. It has often been humbling to my mind when I have viewed taken into view the mercies of providence in sparing him a little longer to us. The appearance of so few faithful laborers, and they removed is very awful and awakening. O, may it have that tendency on many of our minds. I am sensible as an individual there is great room for an improvement on my part.

Our beloved friend Hannah Yarnall attend our Monthly Meeting on her return from the Miamis, and laid before it a prospect of a visit to some of the families belonging there to. And having performed what she had a prospect, her face is turned homeward. Cousin John Haines expect to be her company. I thought an opportunity of waiting favorable by we are all in usual health, and I know of nothing to the contrary amongst any of our Friends.

closer.salute: With near affection to Uncle and thyself, I am thy niece

postscript.p: P.S. my love affectionately to cousin Rachel and Lydia Lippencott and all of our relations
